parole.testo: Inherited from Old French herbergier, from Old High German heribergan, from Proto-West Germanic *harjabergu (“army camp, shelter”). Related to German beherbergen, English harbour.

Inherited from Middle French rider, from Old French rider (“to wrinkle”), from Old High German rīdan, wrīdan (“to turn; twist; wind; wring; wind up; wrench”), from Proto-West Germanic *wrīþan (“to turn, twist”). Cognate with German reiden (“to turn; tie up; lace”). More at writhe.

Inherited from Middle French ternir, from Old French ternir (“to make dim, make wan”), borrowed from Old High German *ternen, tarnen, from Proto-West Germanic *darnijan (“to cover up, conceal, hide”).
